title: add session-snapshot facade + cross-sdk helpers for resumable streaming and debug handoff
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce SessionSnapshot export/import helpers in Python SDK and companion docs and compatibility adapters for TS/Go; minor SDK version bumps and examples showing resumable streaming handoff.
description: Context: customers requested an ergonomic way to capture in-progress streaming context (KV-cache pointer, partial output buffer, credential/lease hints, and checkpoint metadata) to enable safe handoff between processes or cross-language debugging. This PR adds a first-class SessionSnapshot facade in the Python SDK, with companion adapters and semantics designed to be portable across TypeScript and Go. Motivation: teams running mixed-language services (Python ingestion + TS frontend + Go edge) wanted deterministic resume semantics for long-tail streams and easier incident analysis. What this PR does: 1) Implements SessionSnapshot class with to_bytes()/from_bytes() and to_json()/from_json() methods; snapshot contains opaque lightweight state, version header, and optional debug hints. 2) Adds snapshotting helpers to the core streaming consumer so callers can call stream.snapshot() at safe checkpoints. 3) Introduces a compact portability encoding (v1 snapshot format) and a compatibility shim to deserialize snapshots produced by older session-lease prototypes. 4) Adds easy-to-call resume_from_snapshot(session_snapshot) on the StreamClient to rehydrate progress and reconnect with identical retry/backoff windows and KV cache pointers where supported by the serving runtime. 5) Adds cross-SDK reference adapters: a thin JSON compatibility spec in docs and example adapters in redwood-sdk-typescript and redwood-sdk-go so teams can exchange snapshots between services. 6) Updates SDK CHANGELOGs and bumps package versions: python 0.5.2 -> 0.6.0, typescript 1.3.4 -> 1.4.0, go v1.1.2 -> v1.2.0. 7) Adds unit and integration tests covering snapshot fidelity, version negotiation, and resume correctness under transient network failures. Backwards compatibility and safety: snapshots are treated as advisory; if resume semantics are not supported by the runtime or model variant, resume_from_snapshot falls back to a full new stream with best-effort warnings logged. The snapshot includes checksum and version to avoid silent incompatibility. Rollout plan: feature gated behind opt-in runtime flag and SDK feature toggle; will be enabled for a small set of customers after staged rollout. Checklist: - [x] Python implementation and tests - [x] TS/Go adapter examples and docs - [x] CHANGELOG and version bumps - [x] Integration tests with simulated restart - [x] Security review of snapshot contents (no secrets persisted) - [x] CI green Improvements in ergonomics: the new API is intentionally minimal: capture a snapshot with stream.snapshot("checkpoint-name"), persist snapshot.to_bytes() or JSON string, and resume with client.resume_from_snapshot(snapshot). The API surfaces explicit warnings for non-deterministic resume points. Related work: builds on ENG-2359 (session-lease prototype) and aligns with ongoing cross-sdk credential work (ENG-2404).

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Nice ergonomic surface. Please add more explicit docstrings around what is intentionally not persisted (no secrets), and include an example of a safe storage pattern for snapshots.
Aisha Patel: Added docstrings and a short subsection describing storage best practices. Also added a security gating test to assert no secret-like fields are serialized.
Priya Menon: We need to ensure resume_from_snapshot does not bypass auth renewal windows; add a test that simulates a rotated credential and ensure resume fails with explicit error.
Aisha Patel: Added simulated rotation test and ensured resume surfaces a RecoverableResumeError with guidance.
Kenji Takahashi: Approve after small nit about naming of internal _v1 header; prefer 'format_version' for clarity.
Aisha Patel: Renamed header to format_version and updated adapters and docs.
Release manager (Lena V.): Confirmed changelog entry and version bump approach for all three SDKs.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash and merge. Commit message: 'session(snapshot): add exportable SessionSnapshot + cross-sdk adapters and resume_from_snapshot API (python/ts/go)'.
notes_for_backport: No immediate backport required. Feature gated; if backport requested target minor release branch must include opt-in flag and updated runtime compatibility shim.
user_facing_examples: redwood-sdk-typescript/examples/snapshot_adapter.ts — demonstrates deserialize and resume in TS client
post_merge_tasks: Publish SDK packages (python wheel, ts npm, go modules) according to release schedule
Announce feature and docs with opt-in instructions
Coordinate with runtime team to enable server-side snapshot handling flags for pilot customers
migration_notes: Snapshots include 'format_version' and checksum. Older snapshots are rejected with a clear error directing users to a migration tool. No persisted secrets; store snapshots as opaque artifacts in secure blob storage.
